body: What do implementations do today? I'm pretty sure WebKit doesn't have a "set once" special case.

Chromium reacts to `muted` content attribute changes but only for `AttributeModificationReason::kByParser` which can only happen once in [`HTMLMediaElement::ParseAttribute()`](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/media/html_media_element.cc;l=816-819;drc=c45eda2c36eba49623d454c7662e9200e7abcf40).

Gecko seems to look at the `muted` content attribute in two places: in [`HTMLMediaElement::DoneCreatingElement()`](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/f3695d1fd8d9f7419576d8e0366069bf2cc576ac/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#L5376-L5380) and in [`HTMLMediaElement::CopyInnerTo()`](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/f3695d1fd8d9f7419576d8e0366069bf2cc576ac/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#L7367-L7369), which maybe is for cloning, not sure.

WebKit has a tri-state optional bool `m_implicitlyMuted` and a boolean `m_explicitlyMuted`. I'm not sure about `m_implicitlyMuted`, but `m_explicitlyMuted` is used as a once-only state bit when setting `m_muted` from the attribute in two places: in [`MediaElement::postConnectionSteps()`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/f5c6b73309811b7e52d64f8048c77297de445aee/Source/WebCore/html/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#L1149-L1153) and in [`MediaElement::loadResource()`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/f5c6b73309811b7e52d64f8048c77297de445aee/Source/WebCore/html/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#L2012-L2016).

For Gecko, the [`MutedReasons`](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/f3695d1fd8d9f7419576d8e0366069bf2cc576ac/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.h#L1602-L1607) is also interesting and confirms that `playbackRate` can mute in Gecko. Seems like that doesn't fire a "volumechange" event.

cc @whatwg/media for opinions on this. In short, the topic is how/when the `muted` content attribute affects the `muted` IDL attribute, and which changes in the `muted` IDL attribute should fire a volumechange event.

Recent changes here are https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12389 and https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12428.

I see, perhaps observing the `muted` content attribute in the post-connection steps is a good alternative to the fictional "creation time". As that is a well-defined point in time.

That would require changing the `:muted` tests again I suspect.
@annevk that works for me, I've updated this PR and tests in https://crrev.com/c/7857861 to match.

Summary of Opus + Codex review:


### 1. Attribute order in the markup becomes observable

The parser appends a token's attributes one at a time, and each `src` append reaches the resource selection algorithm synchronously via the `src` attribute change steps and the media element load algorithm. The new RSA step therefore resolves the muted state before `muted` has been appended:

```html
<video muted src=x></video>   <!-- RSA sees muted   → muted state true -->
<video src=x muted></video>   <!-- RSA runs first   → muted state false -->
```

The post-connection steps do not rescue the second case: by the time the element is inserted the state is already false, so the hook does nothing. The same applies to script:

```js
const v = document.createElement("video");
v.src = x;                    // resource selection algorithm runs here, no muted attribute yet
v.setAttribute("muted", "");  // too late
document.body.append(v);      // post-connection steps: state is already false
v.muted;                      // false
```

`<video src="…" autoplay muted>` is the more common authoring order, and on `main` neither order matters, because the old bullet was evaluated at read time. This is the same shape as #12854.

### 2. `play()` consults the state before the resource selection algorithm can resolve it

`play()` step 1 rejects if the element is not allowed to play. The resource selection algorithm is only invoked later, by internal play steps step 1. Since the spec's own example ties the autoplay-policy exception to a muted element:

```js
const v = document.createElement("video");
v.setAttribute("muted", "");
await v.play();   // step 1: muted state is still "initial", so the element is not muted
                  // and an autoplay policy can reject before RSA resolves it
```

### 3. Detached, never-loaded elements stay `"initial"`

Nothing triggers a resource selection, so the content attribute never takes effect, and `defaultMuted` and `muted` disagree:

```js
const v = document.createElement("video");
v.defaultMuted = true;
v.muted;              // false
v.matches(":muted");  // false
```

```js
const d = document.createElement("div");
d.innerHTML = "<video muted></video>";  // no src, so no resource selection
d.firstChild.muted;                     // false
```

Also `<template><video muted></video></template>`, `DOMParser` output, and detached clones. This is @smaug----'s [earlier question](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12473#discussion_r3318280849); the RSA read only closes it when something starts a resource selection.

### 4. The post-connection hook does not cover the case its note describes

The note on the new post-connection steps says:

> This is to avoid firing the event for parser-inserted media elements with the `muted` content attribute

...and for a parser-inserted media element that has `src`, those steps never do any work, because the RSA step already resolved the state during attribute append, before the element was inserted:

```html
<!-- resolved by the RSA step during attribute append, before insertion;
     the post-connection steps then find the state already resolved -->
<video muted src=x></video>

<!-- no src at attribute-append time, so the post-connection steps are what resolve it -->
<video muted><source src=x></video>
<video muted></video>
```

So the hook only does work for media elements whose resource comes from `source` children, or that have no resource at all. If that note is the justification for having the hook, it should describe those cases instead.

### On the fix

Moving the RSA step to after "await a stable state" fixes 1, because every case there is intra-task: the parser appends all of the token's attributes and inserts the element before the event loop reaches a stable state, and so do `innerHTML` and `v.src = x; v.setAttribute("muted", "")`. It would need to be the *first* ⌛ step, since the "no media provider object, no `src`, no `source` child" branch ends the synchronous section and returns.

But it makes 2 worse rather than better, since `play()` step 1 runs in the current task, and it introduces an eventless flip: `muted` and `:muted` would read false immediately after `v.src = x` and become true at the stable state, with no `volumechange`.

I think there are two possible paths here.

One path is to continue on the trajectory of this PR, to resolve the muted state where necessary, which would be at least:
- post-connection steps
- resource selection algorithm
- `play()`

This seems like a bit too much complexity to me, so I also want to consider the option of simply letting the content attribute set the IDL attribute regardless of whether the content attribute is set by the parser, by cloning, or by script. The risk of course is that some media is muted that otherwise wouldn't be, do I've sent https://crrev.com/c/8705732 to measure this risk.

I'll convert this to draft while awaiting the data.
